articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas hoy, domingo 25 de octubre: cuándo es más barata y más cara
articles.standfirst: El precio de la luz se abarata un 18.54% este domingo
articles.summary: El precio de la luz se abarata un 18.54% este domingo
articles.body: El precio medio de la electricidad este domingo se sitúa en 111,75 €/MWh, lo que representa una bajada de 25,44 € en comparación con el día anterior, cuando el coste medio fue de 137,19 €/MWh. Esta reducción en el precio puede influir en el consumo de los hogares. A continuación, se analizarán las horas más caras y más baratas para el consumo eléctrico. La electricidad alcanza sus máximos precios entre las 19:00 y las 22:00, formando un bloque continuo de horas especialmente costoso. Durante este intervalo, se registran los valores más altos, con un pico a 243.6 €/MWh a las 21:00. Además, a las 20:00 y 22:00 los precios son también elevados, alcanzando respectivamente 232.64 €/MWh y 245.42 €/MWh. Estos datos evidencian que la franja horaria de mayor coste coincide con las horas pico de consumo. La electricidad es más barata durante la madrugada y las primeras horas del día, ofreciendo importantes oportunidades de ahorro. En particular, las franjas horarias más relevantes se concentran entre las 00:00 y 01:00 con un precio de 196.7 €/MWh y desde 02:00 hasta 04:00, donde los precios caen notablemente a 151.52 €/MWh y 133.26 €/MWh respectivamente. Sin embargo, las mejores oportunidades se encuentran sobre todo entre las 10:00 y 16:00, alcanzando precios negativos de hasta -1.46 €/MWh en la franja de 12:00 a 13:00, lo que sugiere una ventana amplia de precios bajos a lo largo de varias horas. Esto indica que podría valer la pena ajustar el consumo de electricidad a estas franjas para maximizar el ahorro. En el análisis de las franjas horarias de hoy se observa una diferencia notable entre la hora más cara y la más barata, alcanzando un pico de 245,42 €/MWh a las 22:00 y un mínimo de -1,46 €/MWh a las 12:00. Esta variabilidad resalta la importancia de planificar el consumo eléctrico, ya que aprovechar las horas de precios negativos puede suponer un ahorro significativo para el consumidor.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: Anac não vê anormalidade em voos no 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Agência reguladora registrou 35 cancelamentos entre 3.797 voos programados até as 13h deste domingo (25). Associação de companhias criticou o que chamou de tentativas de atribuir a alterações em voos 'qualquer outra motivação' que não seja a segurança de passageiros.
articles.summary: Com taxa de cancelamento de 0,9%, agência e Abear afirmam que operação aérea nas Eleições 2026 segue padrões técnicos de segurança e regularidade.
articles.body:
A Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) informou neste domingo (25) que o fluxo aéreo brasileiro operou dentro da regularidade e sem registro de anormalidades durante o fim de semana do segundo turno das Eleições 2026 .

A agência enviou a manifestação ao g1 após repercussão de queixas nas redes sociais envolvendo cancelamentos e atrasos de voos .

3.797 voos estavam programados para este fim de semana, dias 24 e 25 de outubro;

35 cancelamentos foram contabilizados até as 13h de domingo.

O volume, segundo a agência, representa uma taxa de cancelamento de 0,9%, índice equivalente ao do fim de semana anterior (17 e 18 de outubro), quando houve 36 cancelamentos entre 4.233 voos previstos.

"Atrasos e cancelamentos de voos fazem parte da rotina da aviação comercial e nenhuma anormalidade foi identificada", pontuou a agência reguladora em nota oficial.

A Anac afirmou que, apesar disso, notificou as três principais companhias aéreas do país para que informem, com urgência, as medidas adotadas para a reacomodação imediata dos passageiros impactados .

Em comunicado enviado ao g1 , a Associação Brasileira das Empresas Aéreas (Abear) declarou que os cancelamentos pontuais decorrem de motivos meteorológicos ou operacionais .

E que a segurança e integridade dos passageiros são a prioridade das companhias .

A entidade disse repudiar suposições de que as alterações na programação possam ter qualquer motivação externa ou política.

"Essas decisões seguem critérios técnicos e procedimentos operacionais rigorosos. A Abear e empresas associadas repudiam tentativas de atribuir qualquer outra motivação a decisões que visam unicamente garantir a segurança operacional, valor inegociável para a indústria da aviação", declarou a entidade.

A associação também destacou que todas as companhias associadas estão prestando assistência material e operacional aos viajantes afetados, conforme determinam as regras da Anac .

articles.title: Sebi plans curbs on terminal misuse, graded compliance norms for stock market intermediaries
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Market regulator Sebi is planning measures to prevent the misuse of brokers' trading terminals while also considering different compliance
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Market regulator Sebi is planning measures to prevent the misuse of brokers' trading terminals while also considering different compliance requirements for brokers based on their size, clients and use of technology.Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced the plans on Saturday at the 16th ANMI International Capital Market Convention in Mumbai. He also spoke about improving cybersecurity, testing artificial intelligence (AI) tools safely and boosting trading in corporate bonds."We are developing a framework to put in place safeguards to prevent misuse of trading terminals," Pandey said at the event organised by the Association of National Exchanges Members of India (ANMI).Under the proposed system, compliance rules would vary according to the size of a brokerage firm, its clients and its dependence on technology. Sebi also plans to bring inspection portals onto a single digital platform to make supervision faster and more consistent.Pandey urged market participants to treat cybersecurity as a business priority rather than an IT expense. He also called on them to test their systems and prepare for possible failures.AI safeguards and digital market infrastructureSebi is exploring an AI sandbox in which new tools can be tested safely, while providing innovators with regulatory clarity. The regulator is also finalising guidelines for the responsible use of AI, with provisions for accountability, data controls, kill switches and human oversight, in line with the International Organization of Securities Commissions' (IOSCO) toolkit."We are finalising the guidelines on the responsible use of AI. They will follow a tiered approach, with clear accountability, data controls, kill switches and human oversight, in line with IOSCO's toolkit," he added.The regulator's technology agenda also extends to the corporate debt market. A market-making framework is being developed to encourage secondary trading in corporate bonds, while the next phase of Demat 2.0 will involve tokenised corporate bonds trading in the secondary market.“In the next phase of Demat 2.0, tokenised corporate bonds will trade in the secondary market, bringing better liquidity, lower settlement risk, and faster access to funds,” he said.Sebi is separately reviewing short selling and securities lending and borrowing to improve liquidity and price discovery. Rules for depository participants are also being reworked to simplify compliance and strengthen defences against fraud.Pandey urges brokers to focus on investor risksTurning to retail participation, Pandey said the next wave of growth in broking would come from towns and villages rather than big cities. Citing Sebi surveys indicating interest among Indians in investing in markets, he called on the industry to help investors make informed decisions and remain invested for longer.He urged brokers to look beyond completing know-your-customer (KYC) formalities and pay attention to whether the risks their clients take are in line with their financial resources."You are often the first to see when the risk they take outgrows their resources. So think of KYC as "Know Your Client's Needs." Make it an ongoing conversation, not a one-time form-filling exercise."Pandey said investors who understood the risks of their investments were better placed to make informed decisions and stay invested."A client who understands risk invests wisely and stays invested longer. That is good for the client, for you and for the market," he added.Outlining Sebi's broader priorities, Pandey said the regulator's roadmap centred on simpler rules, deeper markets, responsible technology and wider access.“Our roadmap has four parts: simpler rules, deeper markets, responsible technology, and wider access,” he reiterated.You use AI every day. articles.title: France’s economic woes: Debt nears 122% of GDP, growth forecast at just 0.4%
articles.summary: France is facing mounting pressure on two fronts: growing public anger over the cost of living and an economy struggling with high debt, taxes and weak
articles.body: France is facing mounting pressure on two fronts: growing public anger over the cost of living and an economy struggling with high debt, taxes and weak growth. Student protests that began with school blockades have spread, turning violent, putting the spotlight on the country’s economic troubles and deepening political tensions.The rising cost of living is one of the concerns behind the demonstrations, which began largely peacefully but disrupted schools before escalating into wider unrest and pockets of violence involving young people on Saturday. The issue is not unique to France, but it comes at a difficult time for the country’s economy.France is also struggling to bring its public finances under control. Carsten Brzeski, global chief of macro at ING bank, said “France is not Greece”, referring to the financial crisis that shook the European Union in 2009. However, France has repeatedly failed to meet its targets for spending, economic growth and cost-cutting.With President Emmanuel Macron nearing the end of his nearly decade-long tenure, the state of the country’s finances is also expected to be a key issue in the race to succeed him next spring.France’s public debt nears 122% of GDPFrance’s public debt stood at nearly 3.6 trillion euros (nearly $4.08 trillion) at the end of June, equivalent to 119% of its gross domestic product (GDP).The government has warned that the figure could rise further. Three weeks ago, it said the budget would again exceed European Union spending limits, with public debt expected to reach nearly 122% of GDP, setting a new record, AP reported.The growing debt leaves the government with difficult choices. It needs to reduce spending or raise taxes, which are already among the highest in Europe.Gilbert Cette, an economics professor at Neoma Business School in Paris, described the debt as “enormous”, saying, “France’s entire economic policy is constrained by such a sizable debt level.”Cette said France had shown “talent” in both increasing government spending and cutting taxes in recent years, making it harder to get public finances back on track.Brzeski also warned that France’s approach to economic reforms was affecting its credibility. Writing last week, he said, “Greece’s credibility was destroyed by false statistics; France’s is being eroded by false promises and the inability or unwillingness to start fiscal and structural reforms,”Government spending accounts for 57.2% of GDPHigh government spending is another challenge for France. In 2025, public expenditure accounted for 57.2% of the country’s economic output, according to Eurostat, the European Union’s statistics agency. The EU average was just under 50%.A large share of this spending goes towards healthcare, pensions and subsidies for businesses. With government expenditure already making up such a large part of the economy, reducing it further would require difficult decisions.France also has one of the highest tax burdens in the European Union. Tax revenue and social contributions accounted for 45.2% of GDP in 2024, putting the country a close second behind Denmark, according to Eurostat. The EU average was just over 40%.This leaves the government with limited room to raise taxes further to reduce the deficit. Cutting spending is another option, but it would mean making choices about areas that already account for a significant share of the economy.France faces higher borrowing costsThe cost of borrowing is adding to the pressure on France’s public finances. The yield on its 10-year government bond stood at 4.96% as of Tuesday.Higher bond yields mean the government has to pay more to borrow money. This can leave less room in the budget for other priorities, including pensions, education, healthcare, defence and social programmes.Germany, the European Union’s largest economy, faces lower borrowing costs. Its equivalent 10-year government bond, known as the Bund, had a yield of about 3.4%.The gap between French and German 10-year bond yields has widened, highlighting the difference in borrowing costs between the two countries. This adds to the challenges facing France as it tries to manage its debt and spending.France’s growth forecast falls to 0.4%France’s economic outlook remains weak. The International Monetary Fund has forecast growth of just 0.4% for the country this year, the lowest rate among developed economies.The forecast is well below the expected growth rates for both the global economy and advanced economies. Global output is projected to grow by 3.1% this year, while advanced economies are expected to expand by 2.1%.France’s projected growth is around one-third of Germany’s forecast rate and half of Italy’s. Japan, which has the second-lowest growth forecast among developed countries, is expected to grow by 0.7%.Slow growth makes it harder for France to manage its public finances while dealing with high debt, substantial government spending and an already heavy tax burden. Rising borrowing costs further add to the pressure.With the economy growing slowly and public finances under strain, France faces difficult choices over how to control its debt and spending. These economic challenges are unfolding alongside political divisions and protests over the cost of living, while the state of public finances is set to remain an important issue ahead of next spring’s presidential succession race.You use AI every day. articles.title: Beyond iron ore: NMDC looks to 4 continents for critical mineral blocks
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: State-owned mining giant National Mineral Development Corporation Limited (NMDC) is scouting mining assets across four continents, including
articles.body: NEW DELHI: State-owned mining giant National Mineral Development Corporation Limited (NMDC) is scouting mining assets across four continents, including blocks containing critical minerals, as it seeks to diversify its portfolio and meet the future raw material requirements of industries such as automotive, renewable energy, electronics and steel, according to industry sources.NMDC, which meets around one-fourth of India's iron ore demand, aims to generate at least 20 per cent of its revenue from minerals other than iron ore, its key product. PTI reported.The company is exploring lithium, copper, cobalt and rare earth blocks in Chile, Australia, Africa, Brazil and parts of Asia, the sources said. It is also looking at limestone, dolomite, coking coal and tungsten blocks in the UAE, Oman, Bhutan and Australia.The proposed expansion would help NMDC cater to India's growing industrial sectors, including steel, automobiles, electronics, renewable energy, aerospace and defence, railways and metro projects, the sources said.When asked for a comment, NMDC said, "Right now, we are a 99.9 per cent iron ore company. We aim to help the growing industries in the country with the maximum of their mineral needs". PTI reported.In an earlier interview with PTI, NMDC chairman Amitava Mukherjee had confirmed that the company was working on strategies to diversify into other minerals. He said NMDC aimed to become India's largest mineral mining company and generate at least 20 per cent of its revenue from minerals other than iron ore.Focus on reducing import dependenceNMDC's diversification plans align with government efforts to secure long-term raw material supplies and reduce import dependence across key sectors.Raw materials account for around 65-70 per cent of steelmaking costs, according to the ministry of steel's draft Steel Policy Vision 2047. The draft policy outlines measures to reduce import dependence through domestic mining, expansion of coal washeries, acquisition of mining assets, long-term supply arrangements and the use of artificial intelligence to optimise coal blends.The policy also states that India's efforts to increase manufacturing's share of the economy, supported by initiatives such as Make in India, the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme, semiconductor manufacturing, defence indigenisation and industrial corridors, are expected to drive steel consumption.Sectors expected to contribute to this demand include automobiles, engineering goods, capital goods, machinery, shipbuilding, renewable energy equipment and defence production.You use AI every day. articles.title: How Pepsi fell behind in the cola wars—and then lost KFC
articles.summary: KFC’s switch to Coke is the latest sign of a decades-long slide, and PepsiCo’s CEO says fixing soda is now a priority.
articles.body:
Pepsi has suffered many setbacks in recent years, but perhaps few were as symbolic as being jilted by a long-time partner it used to own, KFC.

The fried chicken chain said last week that it would begin replacing PepsiCo's namesake soft drinks with Coca-Cola products at its 3,700 U.S. restaurants in January. The two companies' partnership stretches back 40 years, since the time PepsiCo bought the fast food chain. (PepsiCo spun KFC off in 1997.) KFC represents a tiny sliver of Pepsi sales, but the defection reflects the ongoing deterioration of the drink's brand power .

For decades, the Coke vs. Pepsi cola wars were a part of mainstream culture, with memorable ads showcasing blind "Pepsi Challenge" taste tests of the two drinks. Pepsi's TV commercials with pop star Michael Jackson and model Cindy Crawford in the 1980s and '90s became part of the larger zeitgeist. Back then, Coke's U.S. market share was just a percentage point or two more than Pepsi's.

It's a very different story now. Last year, Pepsi-Cola had 8.1% of the U.S. carbonated soft drinks market by volume last year, far behind Coke's 18.5%, according to trade publication Beverage Digest. In 2024, Pepsi fell to third place behind Dr. Pepper for the first time and remains there. What's more, sales of Diet Coke and Coke Zero are multiple times higher than their Pepsi counterparts.

Pepsi didn't so much collapse as get outmaneuvered. Coke has reshaped its business around brand building and innovation, shedding its capital-intensive bottling business and successfully betting on faster-growing categories like dairy-centric and protein-based drinks. PepsiCo has remained a sprawling portfolio company where soda was one priority among many, and one that got less attention than it used to. The result is a PepsiCo that generates more than twice as much revenue as Coca-Cola but whose market valuation is only about half as big.

Wall Street analysts say that for years PepsiCo CEOs have turned their attention away from the company's soda business in North America because of what was long seen as soda's secular decline. And it's true that soda sales slumped for 16 straight years. But starting in 2021, the U.S. soft drinks industry stabilized, with Americans gravitating toward healthier and more functional beverages, like those featuring protein and energy additives. PepsiCo CEO Ramon Laguarta has admitted that the still-massive business deserves more attention.

"We do not feel good about the beverage business," Laguarta told Wall Street analysts earlier this month. "So we are putting all the urgency of the business and focus on improving our performance in soft drinks."

articles.title: The coffee bean entrepreneur building a business in Kirkcudbright
articles.summary: Lewie Graham runs a cafe, restaurant and coffee bean roasting business in Kirkcudbright.
articles.body:
The harbour town of Kirkcudbright is probably not the first place you would look for a young entrepreneur building up his business empire.

However, in a cosy cafe over a cappuccino, Lewis Graham - Lewie to everyone, has just been recognised for his efforts.

Along with business partner Robyn Goodare, who is from the town, they took over Feast a few years ago and started the coffee bean roasting business Kirk-Coo-Brew.

And, just over the road, is their Italian restaurant Portobello.

Up to 20 staff might not sound a lot but, in a small place like Kirkcudbright, that makes you a not insignificant employer at the age of 27.

'I took a chance on the whisky industry and I haven't looked back'

The 'wee boy from Whithorn' among the world's most eminent scientists

Lewie - originally from Herefordshire - has just picked up a South of Scotland Thistle award.

He said the region had its own challenges and rewards in terms of running a business.

"It feels quite isolated sometimes - not always in a bad way - sometimes in a really good way, we feel like we're separate from the rest of the world," he said.

"But the middle of winter can be really quiet and hard - it's a lot colder here than it is where I'm from as well."

"At the moment I'm looking for a chef to run the Italian restaurant in the evening," he said.

"I have luckily found someone, but that search was almost impossible without doing word of mouth - there's no way you can put up a job advert online and find who you're after.

"But if I was two hours north in any of the big cities that wouldn't have been a problem at all."

However, he said there were other reasons to be jealous of what Galloway has to offer.

"As soon as you talk to people who are living in the big city, they're like, wow, I wish I was living in the countryside, running my own thing, doing mostly what I want a lot of the time," he added.

Locals, too, whether they have moved to the town or have lived there all their lives, enjoy staying there.

"They will all say that it does feel like living on holiday a lot of the time," said Lewie.

"We get fantastic weather for most of the year - it's never really cats and dogs more than a day.

"Opportunity here is really good because the costs are fairly low, you can make what you want of something."

He is well aware that the south of Scotland has allowed him to try his hand in business without the same level of risk he would face elsewhere.

"If I wanted to do something like this in Edinburgh or in England, it would be double and triple the price everywhere and it wouldn't be accessible," he said.

"So I think what people don't know about rural Scotland is that it is really accessible and there's lots of opportunity.

"Tourism's good here and it's really pretty and I think that means a lot to me."

For the time being, Robyn has told him there will be no more expansion and Lewie said he would only open something that was within "touching distance" of his current ventures and his staff.

"I've started employing people at 24 years old and it's a lot of work, but it's really one of the most rewarding things," he said.

"The job is getting people the job that they want.

"We have incredibly high retention - we don't lose people at all, unless to Uni or school.

"But all of our full-timers have been here the whole time we have, which is really nice - it's their project too."

articles.title: Five IPOs to hit Dalal Street next week, targeting nearly Rs 2,600 crore from investors
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Five companies are set to launch their initial public offerings (IPOs) next week, seeking to raise close to Rs 2,600 crore from the primary
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Five companies are set to launch their initial public offerings (IPOs) next week, seeking to raise close to Rs 2,600 crore from the primary market.The upcoming issues include EAAA India Alternatives, SFC Environmental Technologies, M K Sons Fine Jewels, BLS Polymers and Bombay Coated and Special Steels, with subscription windows opening between October 26 and October 29.The IPOs will give investors exposure to sectors including alternative investments, polymers, steel processing, wastewater treatment and jewellery retail.The companies are tapping the primary market to raise funds for business expansion, working capital requirements and debt repayment, while some existing shareholders are looking to monetise their holdings.Five IPOs to open next weekEAAA India Alternatives: An arm of Edelweiss Financial Services, the company will open its Rs 1,200-crore IPO on October 26 and close it on October 28. The price band is Rs 1,585-1,665 per share, valuing the company at Rs 10,765 crore at the upper end. The issue is entirely an offer for sale (OFS) by the Edelweiss Group, so the company will not receive any proceeds. It has already raised around Rs 360 crore from anchor investors.SFC Environmental Technologies: The wastewater treatment solutions provider will launch its Rs 668-crore IPO, closing on October 29. The price band is Rs 313-330 per share, valuing the company at around Rs 3,233 crore at the upper end. The issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 150 crore and an OFS of up to 1.57 crore shares by promoters and existing shareholders. Proceeds from the fresh issue will be used for debt repayment and working capital requirements.M K Sons Fine Jewels Ltd: The jewellery retailer will open its Rs 275.4-crore IPO on October 28 and close it on October 30. The price band is Rs 153-162 per share. The issue comprises a fresh issue of 1.36 crore equity shares and an OFS of 34 lakh shares by promoter selling shareholder Ramchand Murlidhar Raimalani. The net proceeds will fund inventory requirements for setting up a new showroom in Maharashtra and expanding an existing showroom in Gujarat, besides repaying or prepaying certain borrowings and meeting general corporate expenses.BLS Polymers Ltd: The company will launch its Rs 255-crore IPO on October 27, with the issue closing on October 29. The price band is Rs 142-150 per share, and the offering comprises a fresh issue of 1.7 crore equity shares. Of the proceeds, Rs 77.56 crore will be used to expand its manufacturing facility and increase production capacity, while Rs 89.5 crore will go towards working capital requirements. The remaining amount will be used for general corporate purposes.Bombay Coated and Special Steels Ltd: The company will open its Rs 183.1-crore IPO on October 29 and close it on November 2. The price band is Rs 78-82 per share, and the issue comprises an entirely fresh offering of equity shares. The company plans to use Rs 125 crore to repay or prepay certain borrowings and Rs 15.7 crore to finance the acquisition cost of capital equipment under existing lease arrangements with Siemens Financial Services. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.More companies in the IPO pipelineSeveral other companies are preparing to enter the primary market, including Gujarat Victory Forging, Milestone Gears, Avaada Electro, Swara Baby Products, Integris Medtech and AGS Health, according to merchant bankers.These companies are expected to announce their price bands and IPO launch plans by November 5, ahead of the extended Diwali holiday period in Gujarat. Markets and business activity in the state are likely to be affected by the post-Diwali observance of Labh Pancham from November 6 to 15, merchant bankers said.The upcoming IPOs follow a busy month for the primary market, which saw Jio Platforms launch the country's biggest-ever public issue, worth Rs 30,213 crore.So far in 2026, as many as 104 companies have raised over Rs 1.4 lakh crore through IPOs, indicating continued activity in the primary market. The five upcoming offerings are expected to add to this activity as companies seek to raise funds and existing shareholders look to monetise their holdings.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Nobody prepared them’: The ultrawealthy worry wealth will dull their heirs’ ‘drive and desire’ and so some aren’t telling them how much there is
articles.summary: A Bank of America study found 61% of ultra-high-net-worth individuals are concerned about their children’s motivation.
articles.body:
For the ultrawealthy, preparing children to inherit their fortunes is a long process that is much more than just transferring assets. The responsibility of managing their fortunes given to the younger generation has become a point of concern for the wealthiest families as they age—some are keeping the full amount from them.

According to a June study from Bank of America , 61% of ultra-high-net-worth respondents—defined as those with more than $25 million in investable assets by the study—said they were concerned about their children's motivation. They are taking actions such as supporting their children's business ventures (51%), adding provisions to trusts (41%) and not disclosing the full amount of family wealth to them (36%), the study found.

BofA also found that only about a third (36%) of those respondents say their heirs are "very prepared" for their inheritance.

"Leaving a legacy for my children while still instilling in them the drive and desire to work and be productive" was the largest challenge in wealth planning, according to a UHNW Boomer in the study.

But Matthew Saul, founder and CEO of wealth advisory firm Saul Wealth, told Fortune families that worry their children are unprepared for large fortunes often have not given them enough opportunities to learn.

"When a family says the kids aren't ready, what they usually mean is that nobody prepared them," he said. "That is a planning problem, and it is solvable."

"Whether it is the estate plan, the intention for a family property, or the philanthropic intent," Saul continued, "those are dialogues a family should have together, both during life and about what happens after the eldest generation is gone. There is no benefit to leaving the next generation in the dark."

That approach is being used by more of the ultrawealthy as their families are facing much more complicated futures. Longer lifespans extend the period during which multiple generations share financial decisions, and the transfer of businesses and other assets requires heirs to understand not only how to receive wealth, but also how to manage it.

And Saul says that younger heirs often want to preserve their family's charitable traditions while giving in ways that reflect their own values. They might favor more hands-on involvement or a greater emphasis on measurable impact.

"What matters is how the family handles it," Saul said. "Values can be imposed passively, with one generation steering another without ever saying so, or they can be worked out through open dialogue around shared family values and philanthropic goals and intentions. The point is the collective, the family unit and its mission, not what any one member wants on their own."

articles.title: Foreign investors withdraw Rs 48,056 crore in October as market selling continues
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have withdrawn Rs 48,056 crore from Indian equities in October so far, amid high crude oil prices,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have withdrawn Rs 48,056 crore from Indian equities in October so far, amid high crude oil prices, escalating Middle East tensions, inflation concerns and weak corporate earnings. Despite the heavy outflows, selling eased in the week ended October 23, with FPIs turning net buyers on two trading days.The latest withdrawals follow net outflows of Rs 35,861 crore in September. FPIs had invested Rs 20,200 crore in Indian equities in July and Rs 29,631 crore in August, according to data from the Central Depository Services Ltd (CDSL).Cumulative FPI outflows in 2026 have reached Rs 3.08 lakh crore, substantially exceeding the Rs 1.66 lakh crore withdrawn during the entire year 2025, the data showed.Dheeraj Gaur, chief investment strategy officer at Choice Wealth, attributed the selling to elevated crude oil prices, which surged to around $114 per barrel amid Middle East tensions, as well as weak corporate earnings, inflation concerns, and uncertainty over domestic liquidity conditions.The Rs 30,213-crore Jio Platforms IPO also temporarily absorbed market liquidity, while global portfolio reallocations added to the pressure on Indian equities.According to Anand K Rathi, co-founder of MIRA Money, persistently high crude oil prices and concerns over the earnings outlook have continued to drive foreign investors' withdrawals.While second-quarter results have been relatively strong, higher oil and logistics costs could weigh on corporate earnings growth in the coming quarters. Elevated US interest rates have also continued to make American assets attractive, although steady inflows from domestic institutional investors and systematic investment plans (SIPs) have helped cushion the selling pressure, he told PTI.Why FPI selling eased last weekV K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments Ltd, attributed the moderation in selling to a decline in US bond yields, with the 10-year yield easing from 5.36 per cent to around 5 per cent. The rupee's appreciation to 94.94 against the US dollar and attractive valuations, particularly among large-cap stocks, also contributed to the shift in investor activity.Vedant Gupte, Co-Founder and CEO of investment platform Trackk, said the scale of the outflows appeared less alarming than it might suggest, given that foreign ownership of Indian equities was already at multi-year lows and domestic investors accounted for a larger share of the market.He added that foreign investments through initial public offerings (IPOs) indicated that the selling could reflect a rotation out of existing holdings rather than a loss of confidence in India.Foreign investors remained net sellers in the Indian debt market in September. They withdrew Rs 3,858 crore through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) and Rs 1,332 crore through the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR), while investing Rs 3,737 crore through the general route.US policy decisions, crude oil prices to guide sentimentThe moderation in FPI selling offers some relief, although elevated crude oil prices and broad-based weakness in the equity market continue to pose downside risks.Pabitro Mukherjee, deputy vice president-research at Bajaj Broking, said market participants would closely track the US Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy decision and the Bank of Japan's interest rate decision in the coming week.US gross domestic product (GDP) data will also be a key focus on the domestic and global macroeconomic front. Movements in Brent crude prices, developments in the US-Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, and the ongoing corporate earnings season will also influence investor sentiment, Mukherjee added.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump announces Audi will build $4 billion US factory in Georgia
articles.summary: PERRY, Georgia, Oct 25 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that Audi plans to build a $4 billion assembly plant in Georgia that will...
articles.body:
PERRY, Georgia, Oct 25 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that Audi plans to build a $4 billion assembly plant in Georgia that will produce 200,000 SUVs annually, as he seeks to convince Americans to back Republicans in the November midterm elections.

Trump, who has pressured automakers ‌to move production to the United States and has raised tariffs on autos, steel, aluminum and parts, made the announcement at a rally in Perry, near Macon in ‌central Georgia, where Volkswagen's premium subsidiary intends to build its first US assembly plant.

Last year, Trump's tariffs dealt Audi a €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion) blow as it imports all its vehicles for the US market from Europe or Mexico.

Georgia has ​competitive election races for US Senate and governor and Trump is eager to make the case that his auto tariffs are helping the US economy. Critics say they have boosted vehicle prices and that the trade uncertainty has delayed some automaker investments.

"We are planning to bring our biggest and most premium SUVs, and produce them here in Macon, Georgia," Audi CEO Gernot Doellner said at the event. "This is a long-term investment because we believe in the American market."

In Germany, meanwhile, there has been increasing tension between Volkswagen management and workers over massive job cuts in the carmaker's home market, including ‌possible plant closures in light of rising costs and stiff Asian ⁠competition.

"It is right and necessary to better tap into the US market via a new plant," said Christiane Benner, head of the IG Metall union and Volkswagen's deputy supervisory board chair. "However, firm prospects for workers at all sites, particularly those here in Germany, must be clearly defined and set ⁠out."

She said a final decision on the investment would have to be taken by Volkswagen's supervisory board.

Olaf Lies, state premier of the German state of Lower Saxony, Volkswagen's second-largest shareholder, said that expanded production in the US was an opportunity provided German workers also benefit.

"Growth in America must secure jobs and value creation here and must not displace them," he said.

REPUBLICAN SAYS TARIFFS BROUGHT AUDI PLANT TO UNITED STATES

Audi said ​the ​investment will create approximately 4,500 jobs. Construction is scheduled to begin next year, with production starting in the ​early 2030s, Audi said.

The plant is expected to assemble the Audi Q7, ‌Q8 and Q9 SUVs, a US official told Reuters.

Audi also plans to build 25,000 vehicles a year in neighboring South Carolina, the official said. Some of the vehicles, now built in Europe, would be exported, the official added. Those vehicles will be assembled at a $2 billion plant of VW's off-road brand Scout Motors that is under construction in Blythewood, near the state capital, Columbia, the official said.
authors: By Bo Erickson and David Shepardson

articles.title: Home Depot IT chief says its digital price tags won't give consumers different prices
articles.summary: Home Depot CIO Angie Brown tells Business Insider that its digital shelf labels won't bring dynamic pricing for consumers.
articles.body:
Home Depot's CIO says digital shelf labels won't mean different prices for different shoppers.

The retailer sees the tags as a way to show delivery timing and help pick online orders.

It comes as consumers and lawmakers worry about electronic shelves tying in dynamic pricing.

Well, you and your next-door neighbor should be paying the same price for the same product on the same day.

Angie Brown, the home improvement retailer's executive vice president and chief information officer, told Business Insider that it's exploring a larger rollout of its electronic shelf labels, or ESLs — the small digital placards that large retailers have been using to replace paper price tags.

When asked if those wireless-updatable tags could introduce dynamic pricing , Brown responded, "Absolutely not."

Instead, The Home Depot uses those tags to accurately inform customers when their store expects the next delivery of a specific product, Brown said.

"We love being able to show you on the sign, 'You can get this as soon as the next day,'" she said. "And we want that to be right."

Why those little shelf electronic labels have caused so much worry

Several major brands — including Walmart, Kroger, Best Buy, and Whole Foods — have rolled out electronic shelf labels in their stores.

Consumers have scrutinized the rollout amid fears that stores could quickly raise prices during busy shopping periods or use customer data to show different prices to separate shoppers.

Some state lawmakers have responded to that anxiety, too. New Jersey passed a yearlong moratorium on new implementation of the tech. Maryland passed legislation requiring grocery stores to keep electronically displayed prices unchanged for a full business day.

Concerns have prompted retailers to get ahead of dynamic pricing concerns: Walmart's CEO, John Furner, for example, wrote a memo in September to customers and employees, explicitly stating that the technology wouldn't be used to adjust prices.

"We don't set different prices based on who you are or the time of day, and we won't," he wrote. "We price the product, not the person."

Target also shared a similar statement this month , saying that the company "does not use personal information to raise prices."

Home Depot has been testing the technology for years. In its 2020 annual report , the retailer said it had initially used electronic shelf-label capabilities in the appliances section before trying them in additional merchandising departments.

articles.title: Target is turning the holiday marathon into a series of sprints
articles.summary: The holiday shopping season keeps starting earlier, and Target has struggled in recent years to keep the momentum going to the end.
articles.body:
The holiday shopping season keeps starting earlier and earlier.

Target has struggled in recent years to keep the momentum going to the end.

This year's strategy leans harder into the micro-season trend, with a big push in the home stretch.

The holiday shopping season keeps creeping earlier on the calendar, and that head start can come at the expense of the final stretch.

After weeks of crowds, big-box stores in the week before Christmas can be left with picked-over shelves. This year, as part of CEO Michael Fiddelke's turnaround effort , Target is shifting from a marathon mentality to a series of sprints intended to help the retailer finish strong.

Target's US stores will kick off the holiday season with a major reset in the first week of November, followed by another overhaul in the first week of December after Black Friday.

For the home stretch, Target is picking up the pace with a new micro-season intended to carry the energy through the final 10 days before Christmas.

"Decorating your home is done, then you start going to gift-giving," Target's chief merchandising officer Cara Sylvester told reporters at a preview event in New York last week. "The entire back of the store will be transformed into what we're calling Christmas Morning Magic."

That means this year, instead of seeing leftover string lights and stockings in the seasonal section, Sylvester said the zone will be flooded with fresh stocking stuffers priced from $3 to $20.

Target is, of course, not the only retailer to struggle with late-season momentum that can leave last-minute shoppers in the lurch, but Fiddelke has focused on faster cadence to win back shoppers .

"The holiday season is such a culmination of what the team has been hard at work on all year," he said at the briefing. "It's a hectic time of year ."

Target's chief brand officer Michelle Mesenburg told Business Insider that the company is taking a lot of cues from its recently revamped concept store in New York's SoHo shopping district.

Starting early and turning items over more quickly has been a successful strategy at the SoHo store, she said, as well as a flexible approach to fixtures that keep the store looking fresh through several episodes of a longer season. Now the company is looking to put that philosophy into practice nationwide this holiday.

articles.title: SpaceX, Meta, and other hyperscalers are dropping clues you should not ignore
articles.summary: Clues are piling up about what's next for the hyperscalers.
articles.body:
It's important for investors to pay attention to the clues companies give, even if the market ignores them.

I think this is what's happening when it comes to SpaceX ( SPCX ), Meta ( META ), and soon a lot of other hyperscalers — even when considering the selling pressure late in the week on Big Tech names.

SpaceX strongly signaled it's going to need loads of capital to support its ambitions in space and AI. Some on the Street I have talked with estimate SpaceX will need to raise hundreds of billions of dollars to fuel the business Elon Musk wants to build.

Right now, the market is overlooking the impact on SpaceX's financial statement from a series of mega capital raises — likely coming soon.

More capital put on the balance means more interest payments and more pressure to execute on everything from rocket launches to Starlink. In effect, it increases SpaceX's risk profile.

The market took a first step this week in pricing this in while still praising the company's third quarter.

Then we have Meta ( META ) and its surprise announcement of a new class of stock to power its AI build-out. JPMorgan said a new overhang has been created for the stock until the share issuance occurs.

The thing is, Meta won't be done raising capital. This could be just like the start of SpaceX, needing hundreds of billions of dollars in fresh capital in the coming years. That capital is probably coming from debt markets.

Similar to the action in SpaceX, the market has begun to price this into Meta stock.

I get the desire to focus on the positives with Meta and SpaceX — both have a lot going right. Just don't overlook how their capital structures will change dramatically very soon — and what that could mean for their stock prices.

articles.title: Americans say the economy is bad but keep spending. Don’t mistake the midterm polls for a forecast
articles.summary: Consumer confidence is at its lowest level since 2014, yet spending rose in August. Business leaders make the same mistake with election polls.
articles.body:
Consumer confidence is at its lowest level since 2014, yet spending rose in August. Kari Butcher, Burson's Chair for Intelligence & Insights for the Americas, argues that business leaders make the same mistake with election polls: treating what people say as a prediction of what they will do.

Business leaders are making consequential decisions based on a category error: treating what people say in a poll as a reliable forecast of what they will do next.

Consumer confidence falls, and a retailer cuts inventory. A majority supports a social issue, and a CEO assumes speaking out will strengthen customer loyalty. A company's reputation score holds steady, and its leadership team concludes customers aren't going anywhere. In every case, the poll may be accurate. The business conclusion can still be wrong.

Polls measure what people say at a particular moment. On their own, they cannot tell a leader how that sentiment will translate into purchases, loyalty, employee behavior or investor reaction. Get that distinction wrong, and a company can pull back while demand remains strong, enter a debate its customers did not ask it to join, or mistake the friction of switching for genuine loyalty.

The midterms make this harder. The economy is voters' top issue: 84% of registered voters told Pew it is very important to their vote. Polls are everywhere, and leaders want to know what the election will mean for spending, investment, and what customers and employees expect. A poll showing who's ahead may help a business anticipate the political environment. It cannot tell them how consumers, employees or investors will respond to it. CNN's average of recent generic-ballot polls has Democrats ahead 52% to 42%, but that is a measure of preference, not of what any customer will do next.

As a former pollster, I don't think polling is broken. The question I'd ask of any poll is what decision it gives me enough evidence to make. That means knowing whose views the number captures, what's behind them, and whether people will act on them.

Take the economy. The Conference Board's consumer confidence index fell 6.7 points in September to 81.9, its lowest level since 2014. The next day, the government reported that spending rose 0.9% in August while personal income rose 0.2%. Households made up the difference by saving less: the saving rate fell to 4.1%. Sentiment says people are deeply pessimistic. Spending says they're carrying on. Both are partly true, because people can feel one way and spend another. A retailer watching only the sentiment number would miss that.

articles.title: Industrial growth may ease to 6% in September as capital goods, mining lose steam
articles.summary: India's industrial production growth is projected to slow to 6% in September 2026 from 8% in August, as a steep drop in capital goods output and a sharper
articles.body: India's industrial production growth is projected to slow to 6% in September 2026 from 8% in August, as a steep drop in capital goods output and a sharper contraction in mining weigh on the overall index, according to a research report by Union Bank of India.The expected moderation comes despite continued strength in several indicators of economic activity, including vehicle sales and infrastructure-related goods. The bank's estimates suggest that industrial sectors could see divergent trends, with electricity generation expected to remain strong even as manufacturing and consumer durables lose momentum.The government's Index of Industrial Production (IIP) data for September is due on October 28."Index of Industrial Production (IIP), expected to grew by 6.0% (y/y) in Sep'26, moderating from 8.0% (y/y) in Aug'26 due moderation in sequential momentum though favourable base-effect holds up," the bank stated in its report, cited by PTI.Capital goods growth seen falling sharplyCapital goods production is expected to register the sharpest slowdown among the segments highlighted in the report. Growth is projected at 2.2% in September, down from 16.9% in August. Capital goods include machinery and equipment used in production and serve as an indicator of investment-related industrial activity.Consumer durables are also expected to lose pace, with output growth forecast to fall to 3.1% from 11.1% in the previous month.Manufacturing growth is projected to ease to 6.3% in September from 9% in August. Mining is expected to remain under pressure, with production contracting by 8%, compared with a 5.6% decline in the previous month.Electricity generation, however, is expected to sustain its strong performance. Growth in the segment is projected to increase to 15.6% in September from 12.3% in August.Vehicle sales and infrastructure goods remain firmDespite the projected moderation in industrial production, high-frequency indicators point to continued strength in overall economic activity, the bank said."High-frequency indicators suggest that overall economic activity continued to stay strong in September 2026."Two-wheeler sales grew 33.4% year-on-year in September, reflecting stronger rural consumer demand. Passenger vehicle sales also increased by 23.3%.Infrastructure and construction goods are expected to record improved growth, with output projected to rise by 7.8% in September against 6.4% in August.The bank said public investment and a recovery in private capital expenditure could support industrial activity, even as some segments experience a slowdown.Weak monsoon and supply disruptions pose risksThe outlook for the coming months remains subject to risks, particularly those affecting rural demand. The bank flagged the weak monsoon and cost-push price spikes as factors warranting caution."Going forward, we have cautious outlook on rural demand amid weak monsoon and impact of cost-push price spikes," the report stated.Global uncertainties and prolonged supply disruptions could also affect the availability of critical inputs and weigh on manufacturing output.The September IIP data, scheduled for release on October 28, will provide the official picture of industrial production during the month, against the backdrop of the bank's forecast of slower growth.You use AI every day. articles.title: Cancelled flight tickets: Airlines can claim GST refunds if fare and tax are returned
articles.summary: The GST Appellate Tribunal has ruled that airlines can claim refunds of Goods and Services Tax (GST) paid on cancelled flight tickets if they have
articles.body: The GST Appellate Tribunal has ruled that airlines can claim refunds of Goods and Services Tax (GST) paid on cancelled flight tickets if they have returned both the fare and the tax to passengers and can substantiate the refunds with supporting documents.In the case of Singapore Airlines Ltd versus Kochi Commissioner of CGST & CE, Kochi, the Ernakulam bench of the GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) found that there was sufficient evidence to establish that the refunds had reached the passengers directly and that the airline had not passed on the incidence of tax.The tribunal directed the revenue department to process Singapore Airlines' refund claim within two weeks and pay the amount along with interest.The ruling concerns eight GST refund claims totalling Rs 45.92 lakh for the period from October 2019 to March 2021.During the Covid-19 pandemic, Singapore Airlines cancelled flights and refunded passengers the fares, including GST. However, the airline was unable to adjust the corresponding credit notes against its output tax liability.The GST Joint Commissioner had rejected the refund claims, prompting the airline to approach the tribunal. In its order dated October 16, the GSTAT set aside the earlier decision.Tribunal cites evidence of refunds to passengersThe tribunal held that Singapore Airlines was eligible for a refund of the GST collected from passengers and paid to the tax department, as the airline had subsequently returned the entire fare, including GST, following flight cancellations during the pandemic in accordance with a Supreme Court order.“The appellant airline is eligible for the refund of GST collected from the passengers and paid by them to the GST department, but subsequently refunded the entire amount of fare, including GST, to the passengers, on account of cancellation of the flights due to the Covid-19 pandemic in terms of Hon'ble Supreme Court's order,” the tribunal said.It also concluded that the airline had furnished sufficient evidence to establish that refunds for cancelled tickets had reached the respective passengers directly, with no passing on of the tax incidence.The question of whether a business has passed on the tax burden to another party is relevant to the principle of unjust enrichment, which can affect eligibility for a tax refund.Experts stress importance of documentationRahul Shekhar, partner for indirect tax at Nangia Global, described the ruling as a positive development for the industry, arguing that GST should not become a cost when a transaction is cancelled and the tax collected has been fully returned to customers.As quoted by news agency PTI, he said the decision highlighted the need for tax authorities to assess supporting documents collectively instead of rejecting genuine refund claims on technical grounds.However, Shekhar stressed that taxpayers must maintain robust documentation to satisfy the test of unjust enrichment.AMRG global managing partner Rajat Mohan said the tribunal had allowed the refund as an excess payment of tax in a case where the business had repaid customers but had no remaining outward tax liability against which to adjust the credit notes, leaving the tax with the government.“What decided the case was evidence. Passenger-level records linking invoice, credit note and refund, with settlement data, showed no tax was retained, so there was no unjust enrichment. Taxpayers unable to build that trail, especially for agent-sold tickets, should not assume the same outcome,” Mohan said.The ruling underscores the importance of maintaining passenger-level records and documentation linking invoices, credit notes and refunds when seeking GST refunds for cancelled transactions.You use AI every day. His next line explains how America's biggest bank is approaching the uncertainty.

For everyday Americans, there are already concrete reasons to take those concerns seriously.

Start with Washington's borrowing habit. Meanwhile, the fight against inflation is dragging on.

articles.title: MSMEs remain upbeat despite rising input costs, manufacturing sentiment strongest: SIDBI
articles.summary: India’s micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) reported stronger business confidence in July-September 2026, with manufacturing emerging as the most
articles.body: India’s micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) reported stronger business confidence in July-September 2026, with manufacturing emerging as the most optimistic sector even as rising input costs continued to put pressure on businesses, according to the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI).The MSME Business Confidence Index (M-BCI) climbed to 60.4 in the July-September quarter, up from 59.3 in the preceding quarter, according to the eighth round of SIDBI’s MSME Outlook Survey. The improvement points to a rise in business sentiment, while confidence across manufacturing, trading and services remained above the neutral mark of 50.“The overall confidence remains well above the neutral level of 50 across all three sectors, continuing to point to an underlying resilience in the Indian MSME ecosystem,” it said.The survey found that nearly half of the enterprises covered reported better business conditions during the quarter. Around 49% said conditions had improved compared with the previous quarter, while 33% reported no change. The remaining 18% said business conditions had weakened.The M-BCI measures the current sentiment, health and optimism of micro, small and medium enterprises. The survey’s forward-looking indicator also pointed to continued confidence, with the MSME Business Expectations Index (M-BEI) projected at 61.7 for October-December 2026 and 62.2 for July-September 2027.“Future outlook remains positive, with the M-BEI at 61.7 for OctDec 2026 and 62.2 for Jul-Sep 2027, signalling sustained optimism about business prospects,” it said, as cited by ANI.Manufacturing firms report stronger sales sentimentManufacturing recorded the highest business confidence among the three sectors, with its M-BCI increasing to 61.0 in July-September 2026 from 59.5 in the previous quarter.Sales trends also showed some improvement.Around 43% of manufacturing enterprises reported positive sales growth during the quarter, while the proportion of pessimistic responses declined to 27%.The sector’s expectations for the coming quarters were stronger still. Its Business Expectations Index stood at 63.3 for October-December 2026 and is expected to reach 64.8 for July-September 2027.“Future expectations remain significantly upbeat, with the Manufacturing MSME Business Expectations Index (M-BEI) at 63.3 for Oct-Dec 2026 and rising to 64.8 for JulSep 2027, signalling confidence in improved business conditions ahead.”Services confidence improves, trading and services outlook stays positiveBusiness confidence in the services sector also strengthened during the July-September quarter. articles.title: Rent control doomed this mayor’s re-election campaign. He has no regrets
articles.summary: Brett Smiley was elected in 2022 on the pledge to build more housing in Providence. He lost re-election for opposing rent control, which he thinks is cheap, easy politics.
articles.body: Brett Smiley was elected mayor of Providence in 2022 on a pledge to build more housing and get things done in Rhode Island’s capital city. Smiley worked closely with city and state leaders to relax restrictive zoning laws and cut red tape to make it easier to build. This textbook Yes in My Backyard (YIMBY) strategy was fueling a development boom in the city. Providence added more apartments in its latest fiscal year than in any year in two decades, 40% of them affordable. But there was one policy that Smiley wouldn’t get behind: rent control. Locked in a tight re-election campaign against a democratic socialist, Smiley vetoed a rent control bill passed by the Providence City Council in April. His position put him on the wrong side of a bedrock progressive policy in one of the most liberal places in America. “I believe it is a false promise,” he said in a phone interview earlier this month. “But it’s good, cheap, easy politics.” Smiley lost the election. It wasn’t close. He became the first mayor in Providence’s history to lose in a primary, falling in September to David Morales, a 27-year-old state lawmaker and member of the Democratic Socialists of America. Morales, who called the veto “absolutely shameful,” is a near lock to win the general election next month. Morales pledged to sign rent control in his first 100 days. Struggling renters across America are angry over soaring housing costs and tired of waiting. Many are desperate for quick help in the form of rent control offered by a rising generation of leaders like Morales and Zohran Mamdani of New York City — not Smiley’s hard, laborious approach of adding new supply that takes years to make a difference. Rent control remains potent politically in big cities like New York and Los Angeles and smaller ones such as Portland, Maine, and St. Paul, Minnesota, even as the policy has a checkered history. Rent controls have been shown to limit rents for people who live in regulated apartments, but raise them for people who don’t and push down new housing construction. Smiley, previously the chief of staff to former Rhode Island Gov. Gina Raimondo, took a hard line against rent control. He refused to negotiate with the City Council over the issue. Providence would have become the only city in Rhode Island with rent control, and Smiley thought many developers would choose instead to build in other communities without these restrictions. The bill would make it harder to build the housing that Providence desperately needed, he said. Providence’s housing shortage Rhode Island has lagged far behind other states in building housing since its peak in the 1980s. From 2008 to 2015, builders received fewer than 1,000 permits a year in the state. Providence’s rental market has come under stress from college students and higher earners from Boston, Connecticut and New York moving into the city, said Brenda Clement, the executive director of HousingWorks RI, a research and policy organization at Roger Williams University. Providence also has one of the oldest housing stocks in the country. Many apartments have become unlivable, further cutting into supply. Providence was ranked last year as the least affordable metro for renters. Median rents have increased 40% since 2020. The City Council hoped that capping annual rent hikes at 4% would bring some relief to renters, with carveouts for many landlords. Landlords who live in one of their properties would be partly exempt from the caps on rent increases, and new apartments would be exempt for up to 20 years. Existing apartments also would not be subject to the rent limits until five years after they were built. “I’ve been unapologetically supportive of capping rent hikes at 4% a year because I believe our neighbors deserve that basic stability,” Morales said in an interview. Providence residents “want to make sure that they have a mayor who’s looking out for their interests, not those of corporate donors.” The exemptions included in the bill will help ensure that developers have incentives to keep building in the city, Morales said. Portland and St. Paul were seen as models for Providence’s version of rent control. In 2020, Portland voters approved caps on annual rent hikes tied to inflation. New home construction has continued to grow in Portland after the caps went into effect, but Portland’s mayor has expressed concerns that rent control has made it harder for landlords to maintain existing apartments. St. Paul told a different story. In 2022, St. Paul capped annual rent increases at 3% for most apartments. New construction plunged and rents increased. St. Paul is now walking back some of its law. Smiley and his team studied rent control policies in these cities and talked to leaders. He came away convinced that rent control “perversely would exacerbate our affordability challenges” in Providence. Smiley isn’t sure what work he will do after leaves office. But he won’t be endorsing Morales. “I personally don’t believe that that we should be welcoming the DSA into the Democratic Party with open arms,” Smiley said. “I’m very worried that this is a little bit like the Tea Party on the right years ago.”

articles.title: From brain drain to brain circulation: India wants to become a global talent hub. What needs to change?
articles.summary: By Sebin Jinny For Indian professionals abroad, the case for returning no longer rests on sentiment alone.
articles.body: By Sebin JinnyFor Indian professionals abroad, the case for returning no longer rests on sentiment alone. As global companies build senior engineering, research and leadership roles in India, the argument for returning back has only strengthened.But professionals rarely make the decision on the role alone. For most families, the decision is shaped by compensation and how it compares with what they earn abroad, the tax implications of relocating, the choice of schools for their children, the career prospects of a spouse, and the everyday texture of life, from infrastructure and healthcare to commute and civic services. On several of these fronts, India’s offer has visibly improved. On others, it is still being tested.India’s first global talent story was about Indian capability travelling to the world. The next chapter is about movement in both directions. Indian professionals are returning home, and organisations are bringing in international expertise where it helps them move from investment to execution faster. Making that two-way flow work depends on more than opportunity. It needs clear visa pathways, predictable tax treatment and policies that give people and employers confidence to move.For much of India's modern economic journey, its talent narrative has been strikingly consistent: India develops exceptional people, and the world competes for them. Indian engineers, doctors, scientists, entrepreneurs and business leaders have built organisations and capabilities across global markets.That remains a source of enormous strength. But the conversation is evolving. Companies are not looking at India only as a market or a source of talent. They are increasingly looking to build sophisticated operations here: advanced manufacturing, digital infrastructure, research, innovation and regional or global capability.This creates a sharper question for India: can we become as effective at attracting and deploying critical global expertise as we have been at developing and exporting talent?This is not a case for substituting India’s strong domestic workforce. It is about bringing in specialist expertise where it helps projects get delivered sooner, passing on knowledge, and leaving local teams stronger than before. Skilled mobility is part of a country’s economic infrastructure. It is how eventually an investment turns into real output.India's opportunity at a glanceThose numbers matter, but they do not tell the full story. Organisations investing in India rarely struggle with a lack of commitment to the market. More often, the challenge is how quickly they can deploy the small number of specialists needed to operationalise that investment. Whether it is commissioning advanced equipment, transferring a production process, establishing a new function or training the first local team, the success of a project can sometimes hinge on just a handful of individuals.That is why the talent question should not be framed as “Does India have talent?” Of course it does. The more commercially relevant question is: “Can an organisation place the precise expertise it needs in India, at the stage when that expertise creates the greatest value?”From brain drain to brain circulation Returning professionals are just one part of a wider flow of talent. Indians are coming back after years abroad. Members of the diaspora are sharing specialist knowledge from where they are. International experts are arriving for a defined period to build skills and pass them on. In June 2026, the Ministry of Home Affairs launched the e-OCI card, making it easier for people of Indian origin with foreign citizenship to stay connected to India. That is a welcome step. The next one is to make it just as easy for them to contribute.What is drawing people backThe pull is increasingly professional. India now hosts 2,117 global capability centres employing 2.36 million people, according to the Nasscom-Zinnov GCC Landscape 2026. These centres are doing more than support work. The Economic Survey 2024-25 expects global roles within them to grow from around 6,500 to more than 30,000 by 2030. That means senior roles once held at global headquarters will increasingly sit in India.Senior talent is beginning to respond. BCG’s 2026 research on global talent mobility places India among the top three destinations for STEM and AI talent, and notes that returning non-resident Indians are likely a large part of that.The e-B4 visa: getting factories up and running Returning talent is one half of the picture. The other is expertise that arrives with investment. The proposed Electronic Production Investment Visa (e-B4) is designed to let specialists commission equipment, support production ramp-up and train local teams within clear compliance boundaries. The focus is on enabling businesses to get operations up and running efficiently while ensuring that the knowledge and expertise brought in contribute to building local capabilities. The lasting value lies in what remains behind: trained teams, stronger capabilities and more resilient operations.Global campuses, closer to home India’s effort to attract global capability is now visible in higher education too. The University Grants Commission’s 2023 regulations created a legal pathway for foreign universities to set up campuses in India. So far, the UGC has issued 16 Letters of Intent to 15 institutions from Australia, Italy, the UK and the US, with campuses planned in cities including Bengaluru, Greater Noida, Gurugram, Mumbai and Chennai.This is not only an education story. A new campus needs faculty, researchers, academic leaders and specialist professionals who can design programmes, build institutional systems and connect Indian students with international research and teaching networks.A foreign university that opens a campus here is making a long-term commitment to India. For that commitment to pay off, its academics and institutional leaders need an immigration framework that is clear and predictable.What will make India competitiveGetting outcomes right depends on getting the system right. India should not start by asking how many foreign professionals to admit. It should ask where internationally mobile expertise can create outsized value for its economy and workforce.Companies making investment decisions rarely look at immigration on its own. They ask whether capital, technology, leadership and specialist skills can arrive together and work together. Seen this way, skilled mobility is not an administrative afterthought. It is part of the infrastructure that turns investment intent into operating capability.Predictability matters as much as speed. Businesses can plan around a process that takes time. What they cannot plan around is uncertainty: unclear eligibility, inconsistent documentation requirements, or no way of knowing when a critical person can start.A competitive system is not a permissive one. Predictability gives organisations the confidence to plan, and compliance protects the integrity of the system. Visa policy alone will not decide the outcome. Sought-after professionals and their families weigh the whole proposition: career opportunity, immigration certainty, tax, family needs, quality of life, professional networks and continued access to global opportunities.For employers, this means global mobility cannot operate as a stand-alone transaction. It must connect immigration, tax, relocation, workforce planning and business strategy. For policymakers, it means that attracting talent is as much about the quality and coherence of the experience as it is about the formal availability of a visa.For returning professionals, three measures would make the most immediate difference.First, a single, authoritative guide to the residency, tax and foreign-exchange position of returnees.Second, simpler documentation and post-arrival processes, including banking and registrations, applied consistently across cities.Third, structured return programmes from employers that cover relocation, spousal career support and onboarding, treating the move as a household decision rather than just a job transfer.What this means for the rest of usJobs and skills: Specialists who bring a new project to life also train its first local team. Local engineers, technicians and professionals pick up scarce skills that employers want. And when a project starts up faster, the hiring starts sooner too.Your child’s education: International education opportunities closer to home could give students access to global curricula and learning experiences without the expense of moving abroad.Coming home: The e-OCI card is meant to make it easier for Indian-origin professionals abroad, including relatives and friends, to return, invest or share their expertise.What we buy: Plants that reach production sooner mean more of the electronics and machines we use could be made closer to home.The next chapterIf India combines the depth of its domestic workforce with returning Indian talent and carefully targeted international expertise, it can build more than a large talent pool. It can build a genuinely global talent ecosystem, one in which mobility accelerates investment, transfers knowledge and strengthens long-term capability.Capital can cross borders quickly and technology can be deployed globally. But people remain the catalyst that turns investment into productive capacity, transfers know-how and creates sustainable growth. As India competes for the industries and investments that will shape its next phase of development, attracting the right expertise at the right time will increasingly become a competitive advantage.India’s expanding diplomatic relationships and network of Free Trade Agreements create an opportunity to align trade, investment and talent mobility. India’s next competitiveness agenda should therefore recognise skilled mobility not merely as an immigration consideration, but as an economic capability in its own right.If this works, people will see it in three places: better jobs closer to home, more options for where their children study, and an easier path back for Indians living abroad.(The author is Partner at Vialto Partners. Views are personal.)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Deadlock thaws: IndiGo to start international flights from Navi Mumbai in Feb
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The deadlock over shifting of international flights from Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) to Navi Mumbai
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The deadlock over shifting of international flights from Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) could finally be thawing. IndiGo and Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) Sunday announced that they are in final stages of operationalising a plan for IndiGo to commence international operations from NMIA starting Feb 2027 and progressively expand its presence thereafter.As part of its expansion at NMIA, IndiGo will progressively transfer 12 daily international departures from CSMIA to NMIA, representing all the present operations from CSMIA to Bahrain, Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah, Madinah, Kuwait, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, Muscat, Dhaka and Jakarta. An additional daily service to Kathmandu will also be introduced, taking IndiGo’s international network at NMIA to 12 destinations between Feb and July 2027.IndiGo will also transition the required domestic connectivity from CSMIA to NMIA to support these international services, “ensuring seamless onward connections for customers,” said a statement issued by IndiGo and AAHL. “In close collaboration with IndiGo, AAHL has been working to enable the necessary infrastructure at NMIA for delivering a smooth and efficient transfer experience between IndiGo’s International and Domestic services at NMIA. This will mark the next step of IndiGo’s expansion strategy to build NMIA as a long-term international hub,” it added.“At CSMIA, this capacity transition will also facilitate two additional joint objectives. First, it will create room for IndiGo’s continued international expansion in 2027, enabling the launch of new services across Asia, Africa and Europe using its expanding fleet of A320/321 and A321XLR during 2027, without placing further pressure on a capacity constrained airport. Second, the associated transition of domestic operations will also support IndiGo’s share of the capacity reductions required to enable the redevelopment of CSMIA T1 by 2030. IndiGo and AAHL will continue to work together to ensure that any further adjustments required to IndiGo’s services at CSMIA T1, to enable the redevelopment, will be accommodated in CSMIA T2.”“The phased transition is intended to support a transparent, equitable and proportionate rebalancing of capacity across Mumbai’s dual airport system, taking into account each airline’s presence at CSMIA. This balanced approach will help facilitate an orderly transition for all carriers, minimize operational disruption and provide greater planning certainty for airlines and passengers as NMIA scales up and CSMIA progresses with its redevelopment,” it added.IndiGo will announce final dates for the transition of services to NMIA and introduction of new services to CSMIA after completion of final project coordination and relevant operating approvals are secured.“The phased transition will materially expand connectivity from NMIA and further expand international reach from CSMIA, thereby providing passengers across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region with stronger twin-airport access to broader range of domestic and international travel,” it added.You use AI every day.
